open_points.subject: TrialCase input and expected-output maps
open_points.text: “inputs: StoredValues (M21) by input port” and “expected_outputs: StoredValues by output port ... absent when only the absence of failure is required” do not say whether a present map must contain exactly every declared port or may be partial, nor whether extra port names are refused.
open_points.question: Must trial inputs contain exactly all contract inputs, and when expected_outputs is present must it contain exactly all contract outputs?
options: Both maps must be exact
Inputs must be exact but expected outputs may be partial
Either map may be partial
open_points.default_guess: Require exact inputs and, when present, exact expected outputs.

open_points.subject: Guard comparison
open_points.text: A guarded edge delivers “when that port's value equals” its guard value, and mutual exclusion depends on guard values being “different”, but no equality rule for JSON values is given.
open_points.question: How are guard values compared, especially numbers such as 1 and 1.0 and structured values?
options: Compare canonical JSON bytes
Use JSON semantic equality
Use host-language equality

open_points.subject: File output used as a guard
open_points.text: The proof requires only that the guard port be a `one` output whose schema is a closed set; it never requires `value` carriage, although runtime guard evaluation requires comparing its value with a declared closed value.
open_points.question: Can a `file` output be a guard port, and if so how is its content compared?
options: Refuse every file guard
Compare file content bytes
Compare the file digest
open_points.default_guess: Refuse every file guard during proof.

open_points.subject: Mapped-node aggregate outputs
open_points.text: A15 says “A mapped node's trace is its elements' records; it has a record of its own ... only when it ran no element”, while A13 says the aggregate file-list reference is “stored in the node's NodeExecution outputs” and the aggregate value list is written with the last element record.
open_points.question: Which record durably names a mapped node's aggregate outputs when a non-empty map has no node-level NodeExecution?
options: The last element record also names aggregate outputs
Add a separate aggregate record
Reconstruct aggregates from all element records without storing an aggregate reference
open_points.default_guess: Reconstruct the aggregate deterministically from the ordered element records and store no extra NodeExecution.

open_points.subject: Many-file list references and classes
open_points.text: A13 says a file-list reference “carries the list's class, so an empty one keeps it across restarts”, but M23 represents files only as SpooledFile facts and defines no list-level reference or class; an empty list has no SpooledFile carrying one.
open_points.question: Where are the order and disclosure class of a many-file list, especially an empty list, represented durably?
options: Add a list-reference value with class and ordered file facts
Store list class and order in each NodeExecution port entry
Infer them from the port and element records
open_points.default_guess: Store a port-level list reference containing its class and ordered SpooledFile identities.

open_points.subject: Execution disclosure class with no values
open_points.text: A07 defines an execution's class as “the highest class among the values and files ... as inputs — and for an operation also among its outputs” but supplies no result when both sets are empty.
open_points.question: What disclosure class has a zero-input execution with no recorded output, such as a crashing zero-input function or a no-input/no-output operation?
options: `open`
The node's statically reachable class
Undefined, with failure details always hidden

open_points.subject: File digests
open_points.text: The texts name file `content_digest` and compare file digests, while the general digest rule says digests use canonical JSON; they never state exactly which bytes are hashed for a file.
open_points.question: Is a file digest SHA-256 of the raw file bytes, a canonical JSON encoding of those bytes, or another representation?
options: SHA-256 of raw file bytes
SHA-256 of a canonical encoded byte string
A media-type-specific canonical form
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 of the raw file bytes.

open_points.subject: Sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says function code has “no filesystem beyond its input”, but A03 permits opening any path in “the exchange directory and the read-only runtime” and gives the code a writable private exchange directory.
open_points.question: Exactly which filesystem operations may function code perform inside the exchange directory and runtime?
options: Only runner-provided input reads and output writes at fixed paths
Arbitrary reads and writes within the exchange directory plus reads of the runtime
No direct filesystem API; only Python arguments and return values
open_points.default_guess: Allow only runner-controlled input reads and output writes, denying arbitrary path access.

open_points.subject: Sandbox clock prohibition
open_points.text: A03 says it replaces “every clock ... entry point” and K-02 permits no clock, but its closed list omits CPython 3.12 clock-reading APIs such as `time.thread_time`, `time.thread_time_ns`, `os.times` and `resource.getrusage`.
open_points.question: Does the closed trap list define the allowed behavior, or must every standard-library route to clock or elapsed-time information be denied?
options: Only the written list is trapped and omitted APIs remain usable
All clock-reading APIs are forbidden and the list must be expanded
Only wall-clock APIs are forbidden
open_points.default_guess: Forbid all clock-reading APIs and expand the release list.

open_points.subject: Deterministic function execution and admission
open_points.text: K-05 calls admission “a deterministic verdict”, A03 requires the same implementation and input to yield the same digest, but the sandbox permits observable runtime and resource behavior not fixed by the text, and timeout or resource-boundary outcomes can vary with scheduling.
open_points.question: What happens if repeated executions of the same implementation and case produce different outputs or outcomes?
options: Treat nondeterminism as an admission failure
Accept and cache the first observed verdict
Run cases repeatedly and require agreement
Make no determinism guarantee beyond the listed isolation controls
open_points.default_guess: Treat any observed disagreement as an admission failure, though the number of repetitions must also be specified.

open_points.subject: Resource-limit outcome detection
open_points.text: A03 requires “a limit hit” to win over crash or successful output even if code catches the condition, but `setrlimit` failures such as allocation or process creation can be caught by Python and are not necessarily observable by the parent as a distinct limit hit.
open_points.question: What observable event proves that memory, process-count or scratch limits were hit, and how is a caught limit failure classified?
options: Instrument and report each denied resource operation
Classify only externally observable termination or measured excess as resource exhaustion
Let caught failures proceed normally
open_points.default_guess: Instrument the sandbox runner so each denied resource operation is reported irreversibly, like the sandbox traps.

open_points.subject: `process_count` bound
open_points.text: ResourceBounds includes `process_count`, and A03 says it is enforced with `setrlimit`, but the texts do not say whether the runner and initial Python process count toward the bound or whether the bound means child processes only.
open_points.question: Which processes count against `process_count`, and at what instant is the count measured?
options: All processes in the sandbox including the initial interpreter
Only processes created by user code
Concurrent processes other than the runner
open_points.default_guess: Count every process in the sandbox PID namespace, including the initial interpreter.

open_points.subject: Multipart port names
open_points.text: A09 inserts an agent-chosen port name verbatim into `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"` and `filename="<port>"`, but no port-name grammar or escaping rule prevents quotes, CR/LF or other header syntax.
open_points.question: Which port names are legal in multipart requests, or how are arbitrary names escaped without changing their identity?
options: Restrict multipart-used port names to a safe token grammar
Apply a specified quoted-string escaping algorithm
Refuse a binding only when an actual request cannot encode the name
open_points.default_guess: Require a conservative ASCII token grammar for port names used in multipart bodies.

open_points.subject: Approval request digest for multipart requests
open_points.text: State 0 says approval covers the “fully built request” and “Any difference at send ... asks again”, while A10 omits the multipart boundary from both the `content-type` description and body description and declares that equal logical parts have equal request descriptions.
open_points.question: Does changing multipart serialization or its boundary invalidate an approval, or does approval intentionally cover only the logical parts?
options: Digest the exact wire bytes including the boundary
Use a deterministic fixed boundary and digest its exact bytes
Approve the logical multipart parts and explicitly exempt serialization differences
open_points.default_guess: Use deterministic multipart serialization and digest the exact resulting request bytes.

open_points.subject: Manifest `api_base_url`
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host, while A09 forms the request by removing one trailing slash and appending the operation path and derives `host` from its authority. The texts do not rule on base URLs containing userinfo, a query, a fragment, or unusual path forms.
open_points.question: Which components may `api_base_url` contain, and exactly how are its existing path and authority converted into the final URL and Host header?
options: Allow only scheme, host, optional port and a normalized path prefix
Allow every absolute URL and define component-wise path joining
Treat the configured base URL as an opaque prefix string
open_points.default_guess: Allow scheme, host, optional port and a path prefix only; forbid userinfo, query and fragment, then join path components without normalization beyond the stated rules.

open_points.subject: Admission across kernel releases
open_points.text: A20 permits a new release to change the sandbox runtime and dependencies, while AdmissionVerdict, Activation and Implementation carry no release identity and A04 reuses an existing verdict for the same implementation and corpus.
open_points.question: After an upgrade changes Python or sandbox dependencies, may an implementation continue running under its old cached admission verdict?
options: Pin and retain the admitting sandbox release for execution
Invalidate verdicts and re-run admission under the new release
Continue using cached verdicts under the new runtime
open_points.default_guess: Invalidate admission verdicts for execution purposes and re-run admission under the new sandbox release.

open_points.subject: Changed non-contract release ceilings
open_points.text: A20 says “A new release may change ceilings. They bind contract versions issued after it”, but most ceilings—stored values, spool, service responses, surface requests and paging—are not fields of a contract version.
open_points.question: Which ceiling version applies to existing flows, trial cases, active runs and recovered runs after a release upgrade?
options: All operations use the currently running release's non-contract ceilings
Each persisted object or run pins the release ceilings current when created
Old data is accepted as recorded, but every new write uses current ceilings
open_points.default_guess: Keep existing recorded data valid and apply the current release ceilings to each new request, execution output, response and spool write.
